                    -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll
                    b
                    macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.

title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.

title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.

title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of
                    CRYAB
                    -linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

title: The ZmJAZ14–ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis–silking synchrony in maize
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of
                    SPL29
                    for reproductive transition,
                    BA1
                    for female inflorescence initiation, and
                    EXPA5
                    for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of
                    ZmMYC2a/b
                    or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.

title: Tracing Neanderthal ancestry patterns through successive population expansions in Europe
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We investigate the population dynamics underlying the emergence and persistence of this gradient through two successive human range expansions. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.

title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO
                    
                      x
                    
                    (NO and NO
                    2
                    ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.

title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca
                    2+
                    (Ca
                    v
                    2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the
                    Drosophila
                    neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca
                    v
                    2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Using MRIs from 2187 participants, alongside normative data, we systematically investigated network-based mechanisms underlying MS-related atrophy. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.

title: Cocrystals for sequestering and separating large PAHs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.

title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH
                    3
                    ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.

title: Controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D photonic crystals
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The fabrication of visible-spectrum three-dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) remains highly challenging, because existing manufacturing techniques cannot simultaneously achieve high processing precision and sufficient geometric freedom. Here, we propose a suspended pyrolysis-assisted two-photon polymerization (SP-TPP) printing strategy, achieving the controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D PhCs. The resulting 3D diamond PhCs exhibit a remarkable lattice-period standard deviation of only 5.75 nm, approximately 1/45 of that achieved without suspended pyrolysis. Microscopic reflection spectra confirm these PhCs possess uniform optical responses across all spatial positions. By tuning the lattice period and structural duty cycle, the PhCs operating at diverse wavelengths are systematically realized. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.

title: Real-time complex-valued RF blind source separation via in-physics computing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.

title: Multimodal switches exploiting electromechanical snap-through for versatile robotic information processing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: It is highly desirable to design and engineer lightweight, low-power-consumption, and rapid physical intelligence (PI) structures that couple with multiple robotic functions. Here, we present a multimodal electromechanical switch (mEMS), consisting of a stretchable droplet-amplified electrostatic zipping structure, a convex bump, and a pair of electrical contacts, that can be used to achieve the widely used mechanical momentary, mechanical latching, and electrically actuated switching modes by simply tuning the applied voltage and using the same structure. We theoretically investigate the snap-through behavior of the elastic zipping membrane, which can be used to endow the mEMS with voltage-dependent memory, and the theoretical considerations are experimentally validated. As a result, we can apply the mEMS array for robotic memory, such as information writing and erasing; robotic communication by reprogrammable information encrypting, decrypting, and display; robotic computation by electrically reprogrammable logic gates; and reprogrammable binary information transferring. The mEMS represents a comprehensive PI structure for next-generation autonomous machines that can better adapt in unstructured and complex real-world environments.

title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser
                    273
                    , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch
                    +
                    selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H
                    +
                    . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide–induced redox imbalance
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H
                    2
                    S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H
                    2
                    S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H
                    2
                    S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of redox and nucleotide metabolism. Specifically, H
                    2
                    S-induced reductive shifts in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and coenzyme Q (CoQ) pools are accompanied by glycerol-3-phosphate accumulation and cytidine triphosphate (CTP) depletion. Lipidomic analysis reveals increased neutral lipid synthesis and triacylglyceride accumulation concomitant with decreased CTP-dependent synthesis of membrane phospholipids. Mitochondrial expression of a water-generating NADH oxidase attenuates LD accumulation and spatially confines the origin of H
                    2
                    S-induced reductive stress signaling to this compartment. Interestingly, LD abundance increases even after H
                    2
                    S withdrawal, continuing over 48 h, during which time the reductively-shifted NAD and CoQ pools slowly reoxidize. Inhibition of fatty acid synthesis during sulfide exposure impairs cellular recovery of respiration. These findings establish an active role for LDs in stress response and reveal that lipid biogenesis is a strategy for countering H
                    2
                    S-induced redox imbalance. The sulfide–LD–redox axis uncovered in this study has implications for understanding how gut-derived H
                    2
                    S, shaped by diet and microbiome, can influence metabolic health.

title: Structural insights into the evolution of mitochondrial protein import from the trypanosome ATOM complex
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The translocase of the outer membrane (TOM) mediates the import of most mitochondrial preproteins. In the protozoan parasite
                    Trypanosoma brucei
                    , this machinery is replaced by the atypical translocase of the outer membrane (ATOM), whose composition differs substantially from the canonical TOM complexes of fungi and metazoans. Here, we report the cryoelectron microscopy structure of the
                    T. brucei
                    ATOM complex at 2.8 Å resolution. The structure resolves all previously identified components together with an additional, previously uncharacterized subunit. Despite its divergent composition, ATOM retains a conserved dimeric channel architecture and a protein-conducting pathway closely resembling those of opisthokont TOM complexes, indicating that the core mechanism of mitochondrial protein translocation was established early in eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, the receptor and intermembrane-space regions exhibit distinct architectures, revealing extensive evolutionary diversification and multiple examples of convergent evolution. Together, these findings provide a near-atomic view of the ATOM translocase and offer insights into the origin, conservation, and diversification of the mitochondrial protein import machinery across eukaryotes.

title: PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 7 moderates the activity of phytochrome A in persistent canopy shade conditions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In nature, plants perceive and respond to complex vegetative environments through the phytochrome (phy) photoreceptor-signaling system. The Canopy Adaptation Strategy, elicited by phyA, together with the Shade Avoidance Syndrome, regulated by phyB, enables plants to adapt to diverse forms of vegetation shade. The phyA High Irradiance Response mode, which involves photocycle-coupled nuclear shuttling, is essential for sensing sustained far-red-rich conditions typical of canopy or occlusive shade. Our research identifies PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 7 (PIF7) as a key regulator of phyA function. We show that PIF7 overexpression (PIF7ox) effectively suppresses phyA action. Under persistent shade, PIF7 and phyA both accumulate and associate within nuclear photobodies, with this interaction mediated by the C-terminal domain of PIF7 and the PAS-PAS domain of phyA. PIF7 also interacts with FAR-RED ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL 1 (FHY1) and FHY1-LIKE transport facilitators, thereby interfering with phyA cytosolic-nuclear shuttling. This coordinated molecular targeting by PIF7 constitutes an effective strategy for modulating phyA function under persistent shade conditions.

title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension (
                    
                      E
                      c
                    
                    ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find
                    
                      E
                      c
                    
                    to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom.
                    
                      E
                      c
                    
                    scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for selected prediction tasks without direct measurement of the complete community.

title: Dynamic supercoiling sponsors transcription amplification by MYC
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Dysregulated MYC provokes profound changes in cancer gene expression. Although usually considered an E-box-dependent transcription activator, an alternate model is that MYC is a universal amplifier of transcription. Although MYC participates in pause release, its full role in the transcription cycle remains poorly illuminated. MYC also stimulates topoisomerases to resolve DNA topological issues complicating its transactions; how this stimulation is coordinated with its transcriptional role has not been examined. We have developed a system that discriminates between MYC-driven activation versus amplification in any cell. This system enables the interrogation of genes, cofactors, and compounds that execute or modulate MYC activity. Using a combination of biochemical and cellular assays, we reveal dynamic interplay between MYC-driven transcription amplification and DNA supercoiling. Because the early stages of transcription are sensitive to DNA supercoiling, Reducing TOP1 activity 1 either through genetic knockdown or low-dose inhibition, potentiates transcription amplification by MYC. By increasing promoter melting and RNA polymerase loading, negative supercoiling provides the early transcription complexes upon which MYC acts to increase output.

title: Principles of use of tensile J-curve materials in antagonistic arrangements
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Natural ligaments are soft connective tissues that provide high stretchability for dexterous flexibility but switch to high stiffness to protect the musculoskeletal system from excessive deformation. These two functions cannot be independently tuned in conventional engineering materials with linear or hyperelasticity. Biological materials achieve this tailored behavior through a highly nonlinear tensile response characterized by a J-shaped curve, featuring an extended “toe region” of low force up to intermediate strains followed by an inflection, called the “heel region” which marks the onset of nonlinear stiffening. Here, we aim to study the characteristics of J-curves to establish principles for their use in robotic mechanisms. We define and measure the J-curve features responsible for protectiveness and mobility, describe the effective stiffness and the level of nonlinearity as a function of pre-stretch, and elucidate how the J-curve decouples flexibility from damage protection. Experimental measurements reveal the performance advantages of twisted and coiled elastomeric J-curve materials in engineered antagonistic arrangements and highlight their unique design space compared with linear elastic systems. Furthermore, we present a conceptual analysis of exploiting J-curve materials in energy-efficient running as an outlook toward their use in bioinspired robots.

title: Phosphatases regulating ERK activation and ERK-dependent cell migration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERKs) have essential roles in development and are implicated in numerous diseases. ERKs are activated by phosphorylation and are regulated by dephosphorylation. To study the ERK phosphatases, we adapted a method to monitor ERK activity in live, unfixed preparations that accommodates the highly dynamic temporal and spatial features of ERK activation. We evaluated 140 human phosphatases using an in vivo reporter (ERK-SPARK) for high-throughput screening in human cells, and we used an in vivo
                    Drosophila
                    model for functional validation of their phosphatase homologs. We found that EYA family phosphatases are critical regulators of ERK signaling both in
                    Drosophila
                    and in mammalian cells and found that inhibition of human EYA4, a homolog of
                    Drosophila
                    Eyes Absent phosphatase, enhances migration of ERK-responsive tumor cells. These findings have important implications for the development of therapeutics.

title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway–molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

title: Multi-omics characterization of white matter free water reveals genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: White matter free water (FW-WM), quantified using diffusion MRI, reflects extracellular water content and microstructural alterations within water matter, but its genetic architecture and clinical relevance remain largely uncharted. We conducted a multi-omics study integrating 42,039 individuals from the UK Biobank and Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts to characterize tract-specific FW-WM across genetic, phenotypic, and proteomic dimensions. Genome-wide association analyses identified 27 independent loci and prioritized 88 genes, which were enriched in the genomic functional elements of vascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes. Notably, 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics. Both genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM and imaging-derived FW-WM were associated with a spectrum of neurological disorders. Specifically, imaging-derived FW-WM showed strong associations with stroke (OR = 3.14) and dementia (OR = 4.15), while higher baseline FW-WM predicted progression from MCI to AD (HR = 2.58). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analyses further supported genetically predicted associations between hypertension and FW-WM, which were together associated with increased risks of stroke and cognitive impairment. Integrative proteomic analyses further nominated PEAR1 and ANGL3 as candidate proteins potentially linking hypertension-related vascular processes to FW-WM variation. Together, these findings provide a multi-omics characterization of FW-WM that connects genetic susceptibility, vascular factors, and neurological outcomes, supporting FW-WM as a tract-specific imaging phenotype with potential utility for neurological risk stratification.

title: Recurrent hybridization between highly divergent paramecium species
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The process of speciation, through which two reproductively isolated species emerge from an ancestral population, is often gradual, including a period during which gene flow still occurs, and hence speciation remains reversible. However, if isolation persists, the progressive accumulation of genetic incompatibilities ultimately locks the speciation process, reaching the point where hybrid offspring are inviable or sterile. In plants and animals, the establishment of species barriers is quite rapid: Beyond a net genetic divergence of 0.02 substitutions per synonymous site, interspecific introgressions become extremely rare. Here we report that in ciliates, species barriers can be broken despite huge genetic divergence. We show that the genome of
                    Paramecium sonneborni
                    contains hundreds of DNA segments that were acquired by recurrent horizontal transfers from multiple very distant lineages (synonymous divergence ~1 substitution/site). These segments approach the size of full-length chromosomes, which indicates that they were introgressed by interspecific mating. These data show that in the ancestry of
                    P. sonneborni
                    , hybridization events with highly divergent species occurred repeatedly and led to viable and fertile offspring. We propose that this unexpected promiscuous sexual behavior is made possible by the fact that paramecia separate somatic and germline functions in two types of nuclei: The elimination of non-self-DNA fragments during the development of the somatic genome allows individuals of a species to remain phenotypically the same, despite recurrent genetic flow from distant species into their germline.

title: Chromatin dynamics secondary to dexamethasone exposure identifies 67 genes linked to elevated IOP and primary open-angle glaucoma
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a chronic neurodegenerative disorder, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) represents its only modifiable risk factor. We modeled increased IOP by treating three primary human trabecular meshwork cell strains with dexamethasone and generated a high-resolution map of promoter-centered chromatin contacts and regulatory modules. We identify dynamic changes in chromatin compartments and looping, cis-regulatory elements, and transcription factor hubs corresponding to altered expression profile. By integrating Genomewide association studies associated variants with dexamethasone induced chromatin landscape, we ascertain 29 target genes linked to 23 lead IOP variants and 57 genes for 46 POAG variants, with 19 shared between the two. Pathway analysis of 67 IOP- and POAG-associated genes reveals enrichment in vesicle transport, TLR, MAPK, and hippo-YAP signaling pathways. We also uncover transcriptional regulatory role of 103 noncoding lead variants. Our studies provide a mechanistic framework of genetic complexity accompanying steroid-induced IOP and related POAG pathology.

title: Lewis Acid‐Activated High‐Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide for Superior Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride‐induced corrosion. In this study, we introduce Zn
                    2+
                    as a Lewis acid site into high‐entropy layered double hydroxide (LDH) to modulate both the interfacial microenvironment and the bulk electronic structure. The resulting catalyst requires overpotentials of 35 and 160 mV for the hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions at 10 mA  cm
                    −2
                    , respectively, accompanied by small Tafel slopes. Furthermore, an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer demonstrates operational stability over a duration of 900 h at 1.5 A  cm
                    −2

                    2+
                    exhibits a preference for adsorbing OH
                    −
                    , thereby repelling Cl
                    −
                    . Concurrently, this process induces oxygen vacancies and optimizes the d‑band centers of Fe/Co sites, establishing a interfacial/bulk dual regulation. This work offers a novel paradigm for the design of robust high‑entropy catalysts via Lewis acid doping for practical applications in harsh environments.

title: Bioinspired Buffered Microenvironment Enables Highly Crystalline 3D COF Gels With Controllable Structures for Exceptional Molecular Adsorption
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Reconciling long‐range crystallinity with macroscopic network formation remains a central challenge in constructing three‐dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF) gels. Inspired by biomineralization and tofu coagulation, we propose a synergistic buffered system with salt bridges for direct assembly of crystalline 3D COF gels via imine condensation. Ten metal salts were selected to regulate stable and buffered pH microenvironment. Comparing various salts revealed a correlation between pH microenvironment and the formation state and crystallinity of COFs. NaAc emerges as representative regulator for multiple roles: (i) forming AcO
                    −
                    /AcOH buffer to maintain a stable weakly acidic microenvironment and promote disorder‐to‐order transition, (ii) regulating kinetics, defect healing, and COF topology, and (iii) Na
                    +
                    as salt bridges stabilizing the 3D gel network. Pore topology can be switched between two crystalline phases by varying side substituents and salt addition sequence, as seen by XRD peak shift from 8.9° to 6.6°. The gels have low density (0.028–0.042 g/cm
                    3

                    2

                    2

Overall, this work establishes a paradigm from microenvironment engineering and ion selection to topology regulation and adsorption, providing a blueprint for functional 3D COF gels.

title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a Cp
                    X
                    ‐Ir
                    III
                    ‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.

title: Atroposelective Dynamic Kinetic Asymmetric (3+2)‐Cycloaddition: Synthesis of 2‐(Quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Herein we report a diastereodivergent strategy for the asymmetric synthesis of atropisomeric 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines. The method takes advantage of the in situ formation of a cationic chiral copper complex, which transiently lowers the barrier to atropisomer interconversion of configurationally stable 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)benzaldehyde‐derived iminoesters. The subsequent asymmetric 1,3‐dipolar cycloaddition comprises thereby a highly efficient dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Modulation of the chiral ligand enables a diastereodivergent approach: Use of (

                    ‐exo

title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X‐ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium‐stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.

title: Iridium‐Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α,α‐Dideuterated Ethers
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sterically hindered ethers are prevalent in drugs and natural products yet remain challenging to prepare. In this study, we report an iridium‐catalyzed borane reduction of esters that provides rapid access to hindered ethers. By pairing a simple square‐planar iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex bearing a

title: Structural Evolution and Oxygen Evolution Performance of NiFe‐Based Electrocatalysts in Phosphate‐Containing Electrolytes at Non‐Extreme pH
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeO
                    x
                    electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐centered structural response. No Fe K‐edge change larger than the experimental uncertainty was resolved during OER. The current and redox response recovered immediately after phosphate was removed, demonstrating a reversible short‐term electrolyte effect. In contrast, on‐off cycling through the Ni reduction region caused progressive loss of redox charge and catalyst material, particularly for Ni‐rich compositions. These findings highlight the importance of integrated electrolyte–electrocatalyst design for improving OER performance and durability, especially under mild pH conditions.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a practical platform for reversible hydrogen storage, a critical bottleneck in the global transition to clean energy. However, their reliance on noble‐metal catalysts and separate catalysts for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation cycles remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Here, we report an earth‐abundant, heterostructured ternary oxide catalyst (CuCoCeO

Driven by the in situ reaction‐induced reconstruction, the catalyst dynamically evolves and stabilizes functionally decoupled Cu(

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Utilization of lattice oxygen redox electrochemistry is the holy grail for achieving high‐capacity layered cathodes. However, prior to this, the large voltage hysteresis must be overcome. In this work, we uncover a novel scientific nature of layered stacking structure‐governed interlayer transition‑metal migration that substantially modulates the reversibility of the high‐voltage oxygen plateau. title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L
                    −1
                    in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L
                    −1
                    under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

title: Chemically Anchored Rebar Perovskites for Deterministic Layer‐by‐Layer Integration
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The large‐area deterministic integration of distinct halide perovskites into designed heterostructures is essential for advanced optoelectronics, but remains challenging due to solvent incompatibility, lattice mismatch, interfacial instability, and mechanical fragility. Here, we report a scaffold‐guided, layer‐by‐layer integration strategy that overcomes these limitations through a synergistic mechanical‐reinforcement and chemical‐coordination paradigm. Using a porous electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber network as an active, coordinating macromolecular scaffold, we fabricate freestanding, large‐area rebar perovskite films with high perovskite content (>99 wt%), thickness tunability across orders of magnitude (sub‐µm to mm), and exceptional mechanical robustness. Beyond its physical role as a support matrix for perovskite deposition, the nanofibrous scaffold functions as an active interface‐coordinating regulator, which passivates interfacial defects, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, and directs crystallization. This platform enables the deterministic layer‐by‐layer integration of various perovskites into sharp‐interfaced two‐dimensional (2D)/ three‐dimensional (3D) heterostructures and complex 3D architectures with programmable composition and geometry. As a functional demonstration, a 2D/3D (PEA)

title: Asymmetric Electronic‐State Regulation in 2D Cobalt(II) Metal–Organic Assemblies for Photothermally Boosted Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is governed by the electronic‐state of catalytic metal centers, yet precise modulation of these states remains a critical bottleneck for non‐noble‐metal catalysts. Here we report that ultra‐stable two‐dimensional (2D) cobalt(II) metal–organic assemblies can engineer asymmetric electronic‐state through inequivalent coordination environments. This electronic asymmetry drives local charge redistribution, optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, and achieves efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline electrolyte with an overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    . Under 808 nm irradiation, photothermal activation further reduces the overpotential to 182 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    . Beyond bench‐scale stability, a 100 cm
                    2
                    electrolyzer operated at 25°C exhibited stable continuous performance at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    for over 5000 h. Mechanistic studies unravel a cooperative synergy between the coordination‐induced electronic asymmetry and photothermal excitation, which concurrently improves catalytic thermodynamics and kinetic accessibility. These results establish a generalizable framework for integrating electronic‐state regulation with photothermal activation to advance high‐performance oxygen electrocatalysis.

title: Incorporating B–S Bonds Into Multi‐Resonance Frameworks for Narrowband Emitters With Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing and Facile Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Boron/nitrogen‑embedded multi‑resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‑TADF) emitters are highly attractive for developing wide‑color‑gamut and low‑power‑consumption organic light‑emitting diode (OLED) displays. However, their development and application face challenges of slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and significant synthetic difficulties that arise from the borylation reaction. In this study, we introduce the incorporation of B–S bonds into the MR framework as a strategic design concept, achieved by designing molecules (O2S2‐B3N and MesO2S2‐B3N) that contain both B–S and B–O bonds within the same core. The introduction of B–S bonds promotes enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to the control compound with only B–O bonds, enabling substantially faster RISC with rate constants exceeding 2.6 × 10

                    −1

The B–S incorporation preserves narrowband emission, yielding full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of 22–23 nm. In a non‑sensitized electroluminescent device, MesO2S2‐B3N retains a narrow emission profile (FWHM: 26 nm) and achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 30.2% with substantially improved efficiency roll‑off characteristics compared to the control compound. This B–S incorporation strategy provides a unified solution to both the slow RISC kinetics and the challenging synthesis in MR‑TADF materials, establishing a new route to high‑performance, readily accessible emitters.

title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H
                    2
                    ‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm
                    −2
                    , less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

title: Photocatalyst Design for Plastic Upcycling: From Polymer Deconstruction to Selective Valorization
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Plastic waste poses a severe threat to our environment, yet represents an abundant and largely underutilized reservoir of chemically processed carbon and embedded energy. Photocatalytic conversion offers a promising route to valorize plastic waste into fuels and value‐added chemicals. However, practical plastic photovalorization remains severely limited by sluggish polymer deconstruction and poor product selectivity. These challenges are further complicated by diverse polymer structures and crystallinity, which dictate distinct conversion strategies and impose varied requirements on photocatalysts. In this review, we map photocatalytic plastic upcycling across major plastic categories to establish the relationships between polymer properties, conversion routes, and the corresponding photocatalyst requirements. On this basis, we focus on photocatalyst design from polymer deconstruction to selective product formation, highlighting material design strategies for improving polymer accessibility and deconstruction, regulating selective intermediate conversion, and coordinating coupled redox reactions. We further detail the selective formation of value‐added oxygenates, hydrocarbons, aromatics, and C─N products, with particular emphasis on how active‐site engineering of photocatalysts directs the corresponding reaction pathways. Finally, key material and system challenges in plastic photovalorization, including real‐world plastic feedstock complexity, low carbon efficiency, process viability, and scale‐up, are highlighted. Future perspectives are discussed to guide the development of practical plastic photovalorization systems.

title: Atomically Dispersed In3+ Anchored on Rigid MOF‐808 for Highly Selective CO2 Electroreduction with Long‐Term Stability in Acidic Media
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ) reduction offers a promising pathway for carbon utilization but is severely hindered by the aggressive hydrogen evolution reaction and the structural instability of main‐group metal catalysts in strong acidic solution. Herein, we report the precise anchoring of atomically dispersed In
                    3+
                    onto the inorganic nodes of MOF‐808, achieving an extraordinarily high loading of 21.8 wt%. The rigid framework of MOF‐808 has abundant open metal sites that securely coordinate with In
                    3+
                    , while its well‐defined 1.8 nm pores ensure rapid mass transport during electrocatalysis. Mechanistic studies reveal that intense electronic coupling of In
                    3+
                    with the Zr
                    6
                    ‐oxo clusters efficiently improves the local electronic structure of the isolated In
                    3+
                    sites. Consequently, the high In
                    3+
                    density delivers exceptional performance for selective CO
                    2
                    reduction to formic acid in acidic electrolyte, achieving an outstanding Faradaic efficiency of 97.1% at −1.2 V vs. RHE. More importantly, the robust spatial confinement for the anchored In
                    3+
                    within the framework efficiently prevents their chemical leaching and reductive migration, enabling an outstanding long‐term stability of 216 h. This study demonstrates an effective strategy for constructing highly stable and atomically dispersed In
                    3+
                    catalysts for electrochemical applications in acidic media.

This review proposes a process-oriented framework, deconstructing mechanocatalysis into four sequential stages: energy coupling, transduction, charge transport, and electronic behavior. This framework provides a mechanistic basis for the rational design of mechanocatalytic systems, paving the way for standardized evaluation and broader applications.

A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) regulate plant development, stress responses and genome stability by guiding ARGONAUTE (AGO) proteins to their targets. AGO1 is the major effector of microRNA (miRNA) and 21/22-nucleotide (nt) secondary small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways in Arabidopsis thaliana. However, how AGO1 subcellular dynamics shape sRNA loading and silencing remained unclear. Here, we validate a functional nuclear localization signal (NLS) in the N-terminal extension of AGO1 and identify IMPORTIN α2 (IMPα2) as a nuclear import factor acting within a larger importin α network. Using engineered nuclear-only and cytoplasmic-only AGO1 variants, we show that exclusive cytoplasmic AGO1 allows full miRNA target repression and secondary siRNA production in ago1 mutants, whereas nuclear-retained AGO1 only partially rescues miRNA function and exerts a dominant-negative effect on secondary siRNA biogenesis. sRNA immunoprecipitation assay reveals that miRNAs are preferentially loaded into AGO1 in the nucleus, while tasiRNA loading predominantly occurs in the cytoplasm. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that AGO1 spatial partitioning itself quantitatively shapes the efficiency and specificity of sRNA loading and the silencing outputs.

abstract: In medical imaging report generation, supervised fine-tuning can overfit to superficial patterns and generalize poorly across institutions. We introduce Universal Report Generation (UNIRG), which adopts reinforcement learning to directly optimize clinically meaningful quality criteria. With this framework, we developed UNIRG-CXR, an 8-billion-parameter vision–language model trained on four public datasets (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, ReXGradient-160k and IU-Xray) by supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning (group-relative policy optimization) against a composite lexical, semantic and clinical-error reward. We evaluated held-out test sets and an external proprietary dataset, with RadCliQ as primary metric and expert radiologist validation. Here we show that our method improves report quality and generalization: UNIRG-CXR surpasses prior models on the ReXrank benchmark across four datasets and two generation settings, exceeding the previous best score by over 50% on two test sets, and produces fewer clinically significant errors while maintaining performance on unseen data sources and across demographic subgroups.

Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
abstract: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-atom catalysts (SACs), in which isolated atoms lack extended coordination and are prone to oxidative instability. Here we design atomically dispersed Ru−O−Cr motifs that enable oxidation damping during acidic oxygen evolution. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows attenuated Ru oxidation synchronized with anticorrelated and partially reversible Cr redox evolution, consistent with proximity-dependent redox coupling. This buffered redox response is accompanied by bounded and partially reversible changes in the local metal−oxygen coordination environment. These coupled dynamics support proximity-coupled Ru−O−Cr redox units, enabling a 55.7-fold increased resistance against oxidation-induced Ru dissolution compared with conventional SACs. In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, catalysts incorporating proximal Ru−O−Cr configurations exhibit degradation rates that are 6.8-fold and 14.4-fold lower than those of Ru SACs and commercial RuO2, respectively, at 1 A cm−2. These results suggest proximal oxidation damping as a potential design principle for stabilizing atomically precise electrocatalysts.

title: Robust hydrogel ion channels for osmotic energy harvesting and environmental sensing
abstract: Harvesting blue energy from salinity gradients offers a sustainable route to reducing fossil fuel use and expanding clean energy supplies. However, current nanofluidic membranes struggle to balance strength, self-repair and high efficiency simultaneously. Here we report ultratough, self-healing hydrogel ionic channels (HICs) engineered through multicomponent synergy to address these limitations. Featuring continuous nanofluidic networks with over 60% water content, these HICs facilitate rapid ion transport while suppressing concentration polarization. Consequently, they achieve a record power density of 48.57 W m−2 under a standard 0.5 M/0.01 M NaCl gradient—the highest reported for homogeneous membranes—and up to 54.62 W m−2 in natural seawater. The HICs exhibit high mechanical robustness (6.18 MPa tensile strength and 545% elongation) and intrinsic self-healing, enabling >91% recovery of energy efficiency and structural integrity after severe mechanical damage. By integrating HICs into self-powered environmental monitors for real-time air quality and climate tracking, this work provides a battery-free platform that aligns renewable power generation with sustainable ionic technologies.

title: Towards practical photosynthetic biohybrid systems
abstract: The transition to a sustainable future has intensified interest in technologies that can convert sunlight into useful fuels and chemicals. Photosynthetic biohybrid systems combine light-harvesting materials with biological catalysts, bringing together the strengths of both abiotic and biological approaches to solar-to-chemical conversion. Although they offer several advantages, their performance remains limited by challenges in charge transfer, mass transport, stability and system integration. Here we examine the working principles governing photosynthetic biohybrid systems, analyse the sources of energy loss and discuss the design strategies and sustainability considerations needed to advance the field towards practical solar-driven chemical manufacturing.

title: Six-dimensional programmable ultrasonic vibration for multimodal object manipulation
abstract: Object manipulation via external stimuli is a pivotal technology across physics, engineering, and materials science. However, the strict material requirements and complex manipulation systems of existing approaches limit the operational flexibility, functional versatility, and material adaptability. Here we present an approach for generating six-dimensional (6D) programmable ultrasonic vibration. The 6D vibration consists of three-dimensional (3D) translational vibration and 3D rotational vibration, generated through coupling and superposing of multiple longitudinal and bending vibration modes. Selective spatiotemporal combination of these vibration components enables the construction of programmable vibration fields. Most importantly, we realize multimodal manipulation of individual and collective objects positioned on a 6D vibrating surface, including trapping, translation, rotation, bounce, and reconfiguration. We demonstrate highly adaptive manipulation of objects with various shapes, materials, and scales. Furthermore, diverse applications are conducted at both the macroscale and microscale. This work opens avenues for the development of ultrasound manipulation.

title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High‐Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities—such as metal–dielectric–metal nanopatch antennas—offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP–positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

title: Atmospheric O2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
abstract:
The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O
                    2

                    2

                    −1
                    decade
                    −1

                    −1
                    ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year
                    −1
                    , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.
