title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis
abstract: Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth’s viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
abstract:
Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the
                    T
                    2
                    dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime, theoretically predicted to be generic for two-dimensional electron systems.

title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
abstract:
The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ) ice in both the
                    12
                    CO
                    2
                    and
                    13
                    CO
                    2
                    isotopologues. We infer that the CO
                    2
                    ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of
                    meta
                    ‐ and
                    para
                    ‐substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron‐donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron‐withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom‐to‐boron donation, and π‐acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron‐containing reagents and functional molecules.

title: MgO Facets as Regenerable Molecular Oxygen Reservoirs in Oxidative Coupling of Methane
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface‐sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}‐faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis,
                    operando
                    Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface‐bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C
                    2+
                    formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well‐designed surface structures.

title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
abstract:
Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of
                    Drosophila melanogaster
                    during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4+ T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
abstract:
Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T
                    H
                    1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4
                    +

                    H
                    1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding
                    Il7r
                    +

                    +
                    intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T
                    H
                    1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8
                    +
                    effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4
                    +

title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport–0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III–independent reverse-topology budding.

                    stores, diminished Ca
                    2+
                    release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human
                    TMEM184B
                    mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca
                    2+
                    transport, and
                    Tmem184b
                    -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca
                    2+
                    uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
abstract:
The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA,
                    https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/
                    ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent
                    TP53
                    ,
                    PIK3CA
                    ,
                    PTEN
                    ,
                    SETD2
                    ,
                    MAP3K14
                    , and
                    FAT4
                    alterations; copy number events included
                    MYC
                    amplifications and
                    PTEN
                    deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.
